headline: High: open-webui can feed untrusted web/MCP content into pipecat’s shared bus, creating prompt-injection, data-leakage, and cascading-action risks by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: open-webui explicitly ingests browser, MCP, and file content, and pipecat runs on a shared bus with text/conversation state. That creates a direct pathway for attacker-controlled content from agent A to be treated as instructions by agent B. No provenance or isolation is documented, so uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF open-webui forwards browser or MCP output into pipecat inputs without provenance tags
IF pipecat parses shared-bus text as instructions or tool directives
mitigations: Disable MCP and browser-fed inputs in open-webui for shared sessions
Insert a provenance filter that strips instructions from retrieved content
Route A and B through separate buses or queues
Add a manual review step before B consumes A-generated text
requires-engineering: enforce content-type separation at the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: open-webui touches API keys, files, documents, notes, and persistent memory, while pipecat handles text, conversation state, audio/video/images, and can call third-party STT/LLM/TTS services. If they share a workspace or bus, sensitive content from A can flow into B and then out to external APIs. The allowlisted egress on B does not eliminate leakage risk.
conditions: IF open-webui and pipecat share files, memory, or bus payloads
IF pipecat is configured to send conversation context to external STT/LLM/TTS providers
mitigations: Separate storage for A and B data classes
Remove secrets and API keys from any shared workspace
Restrict pipecat provider configs to local-only endpoints
Shorten retention on shared transcripts and artifacts
requires-engineering: add field-level redaction before handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: open-webui has broad network egress, browser, subprocess, and file access; pipecat has shared-bus concurrency and allowlisted egress. Their mutable surfaces overlap on text/state and potentially files, so concurrent writes or state races are plausible. The profiles do not prove same-directory writes, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same workspace, bus topic, or artifact path
IF either agent mutates shared conversation state without locking
mitigations: Assign distinct workspaces per agent
Use per-agent queue/topic names
Turn on optimistic-lock or version checks for shared state
Avoid concurrent writes to the same artifact path
requires-engineering: add distributed locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: open-webui can generate or transform web/MCP content, and pipecat is a real-time framework that can consume text/conversation state and drive downstream STT/LLM/TTS or transport actions. If B treats A’s output as authoritative, errors or malicious instructions can cascade into spoken or transmitted actions. The interaction is inferred from docs, so uncertainty keeps confidence below direct-observation levels.
conditions: IF pipecat uses open-webui output as the source of truth for prompts or actions
IF downstream transports or services execute B’s generated content without verification
mitigations: Require schema validation on A-to-B payloads
Add a human approval gate before any external action
Log and diff A output against B input
Limit B to summarization rather than action-taking
requires-engineering: implement verification against source documents

E_compliance.rationale: open-webui handles API keys, documents, notes, calendar events, and persistent memory, while pipecat handles conversation state plus audio/video/images and may route data to third-party providers. The pair creates a plausible retention and residency mismatch risk, but the profiles do not specify jurisdictions or certifications, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into shared transcripts, memory, or artifacts
IF B’s provider settings retain or export data longer than A’s policy allows
mitigations: Document a shared retention policy
Exclude regulated data from shared sessions
Disable analytics/telemetry where possible
Review provider DPAs before enabling external services
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing and deletion workflows
